articles.title: The website that created an AI clone of its editor in chief
articles.titleZh: AI 克隆了主编的品味，编辑还能保住工作吗？
articles.author: Casey Newton

substance.note: The piece argues that AI automation paradoxically increases demand for human experts, and supports this with a concrete mechanism — AI trained on the residue of human expertise produces slop that requires experts to fix — and a specific example of cloning an editor's taste via 30,000 edits. The mechanism generalizes to any knowledge-work domain, not just media.

surprise.note: Overturns the belief that automating everything reduces headcount, with the counterintuitive claim that 'almost every writer is using it' AI but not saying so — a sentence readers would repeat. Also the specific detail of back-testing an editor's 30,000 edits to create a copy-editing agent is a striking, quotable fact.

accessible.note: The interview format and plain language make it followable for a general audience; terms like 'vibe check' and 'back-testing' are explained in context, and the oven/soufflé analogy makes the core idea vivid without jargon.

relevance.note: The reader who writes, edits, or works in any knowledge industry will reconsider how they use AI and whether their job is threatened — the piece directly addresses the reader's own work and tools, not just a distant industry.

quality.note: The interview is well-structured with a clear arc from vibe checks to the AI paradox, and every claim is supported by specific examples (30,000 edits, doubling headcount, the oven analogy). However, the middle section on the AI paradox repeats the same point about experts being needed in slightly different forms, and the closing podcast plug is tangential.

zh.thesis: 一家媒体公司用 AI 复制主编的编辑品味，让 AI 处理大部分工作，但反而需要更多人类专家来修正和提升。
zh.text:
作者采访了 Every 公司的 CEO Dan Shipper。这家公司既做科技媒体，又用 AI 开发产品，员工仅 30 人，却运营着 6 个软件产品和每日 newsletter。

Shipper 说，AI 现在几乎写了公司所有的代码，但文章仍由人类主笔。不过，AI 正在改变写作流程：他们用主编 Kate Lee 的 3 万条历史编辑记录训练出一个 AI 编辑代理，能自动在 Google Docs 里给出修改建议，再经 Kate 校对后自动学习改进。

## 1. 为什么 AI 没有取代人，反而让人更忙？

AI 只会解决已解决的问题，但它面对的具体问题总有偏差，于是产生大量“slop”（垃圾内容）。这时就需要专家介入，把 AI 的输出调整到正确。因此，尽管 Every 拼命自动化，员工还是从 15 人翻倍到 30 人。

## 2. AI 写作之争：文字算谁的？

Shipper 认为，只要文字代表你的想法，哪怕不是亲手敲的，也算你的。就像用编辑器接受修改建议一样。他预测，未来作者会越来越多地使用 AI，但真正好的作家会用 AI 打磨自己的品味，而不是被 AI 带着走。

## 3. 媒体公司的护城河：当公正的裁判

Every 经常评测 AI 模型，有时会给出批评性意见，这会影响与模型公司的关系。但 Shipper 认为，他们的价值正在于提供客观评价，因为模型公司不可能自卖自夸。他比喻说，模型公司是烤箱制造商，而 Every 是糕点师——拿烤箱做出好蛋糕。

总结：AI 不会让专家失业，反而会让专家更有价值；写作的终极标准是“想法是你的”，而不是“字是你打的”。

articles.title: Why Human Giants Defy the Laws of Physics
articles.titleZh: 巨人为什么不存在？伽利略用一根木梁说清了物理法则
articles.author: Joel David Hamkins

substance.note: The article argues that scaled-up humanoid giants are physically impossible because strength scales with the square of the linear factor while weight scales with the cube, and it extends this mechanism to explain the stocky build of elephants and the slender build of insects, showing the principle generalizes across biology.

surprise.note: It overturns the common belief that a giant is just a bigger human, and the sentence 'if his height be increased inordinately he will fall and be crushed under his own weight' is one a reader would repeat.

accessible.note: The only technical terms are 'cross-sectional area' and 'volume,' both explained in plain language with the oak beam example, so a non-specialist can follow the argument without prior physics knowledge.

relevance.note: The reader will not change any personal action, but the article connects to a system they live inside—the physical world and the size of animals they see—making them feel the scale effects in everyday life.

quality.note: The structure is clean, with the oak beam example, the giant application, and the animal examples each serving a distinct purpose, and the Galileo quote is well-integrated, though the final paragraph on evolution is a bit of a tangent.

zh.thesis: 传说里的巨人不可能存在，因为按比例放大后，骨骼的承重能力只按平方增长，而体重按立方增长，巨人会被自己的重量压垮。
zh.text:
传说中，巨人跟人类长一个样，只是大了好几倍。但伽利略在1638年就说：这种巨人，物理上根本不可能存在。

他让读者想象一根粗木梁，能撑住一大摞砖头。再把木梁按比例放大10倍——长、宽、高都变成10倍。

## 1. 强度涨得慢，体重涨得快

木梁的承重能力取决于横截面积，面积按线性尺寸的平方增长。10倍大的木梁，横截面积是原来的100倍，所以强度是原来的100倍。

但砖头的重量取决于体积，体积按立方增长。10倍大的砖头，重量是原来的1000倍。

100倍强度对上1000倍重量——木梁只能撑起原来十分之一的负荷。再放大下去，木梁连自己的重量都撑不住。

## 2. 巨人的骨头，撑不起巨人的体重

人的骨头就像木梁，强度跟横截面积有关，但体重跟体积有关。如果巨人只是普通人的等比例放大版，他的骨头强度只增加了平方倍，而体重增加了立方倍。

结果就是：巨人走两步，腿骨就会断，然后被自己的重量压垮。伽利略说，巨人要么得换更硬的骨头材料，要么就承认自己比普通人弱得多。

放大版的梯子、刀剑、铠甲、房子、椅子统统同理——全都撑不住自己。

## 3. 反过来看：为什么大象腿粗，蚂蚁能上墙

这套逻辑也解释了动物的体型差异。大象比猫狗腿粗得多，因为体重按立方涨，骨头必须按比例加粗才能撑住。

而小动物则相反：缩小10倍，强度变成1/100，体重变成1/1000，所以相对力量反而大。跳蚤能跳老高，蚂蚁能扛重物，都是这个道理。

水黾能站在水面上，是因为表面张力对它们来说够强；要是放大到人那么大，早就沉下去了。

反过来，小人国的人也一样不真实：他们应该能轻松背起好几个自己，但会被静电粘在墙上，水对他们来说黏得像胶水。

所以，巨人只能是传说。我们人类这个尺寸，本身就是物理法则筛选出来的最优解。

articles.title: Pluralistic: The actual epistemic crisis (20 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: AI 骗不了你，除非你早就被骗惯了
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

substance.note: The author argues that AI's epistemic threat is an opportunistic infection exploiting a pre-existing decline in truth-assessment systems caused by regulatory capture, and supports this with specific examples like the FDA and OxyContin, banks' phishing-like behavior, and celebrity crypto endorsements. The mechanism—that a compromised epistemic immune system makes new lies more effective—generalizes beyond AI to any new deception technology, but the argument is built from a single line of reasoning and examples rather than multiple angles.

surprise.note: The piece reframes the AI deepfake crisis as not a new battle but the latest barrage in a long war of regulatory capture, which is a counterintuitive angle. The key sentence is: 'It's not so much that AI is a powerful way of lying – rather, we have been made progressively more vulnerable to lies for decades, leaving us at an epistemic death's door, and AI has arrived to deliver the coup de grace.' This is a specific, quotable line that overturns the common belief that AI is the root cause.

accessible.note: The article explains the concept of regulatory capture and epistemic crisis in plain language, using relatable examples like bank calls and celebrity endorsements. The only technical term, 'epistemic,' is used in a way that is clear from context, and the Surkov anecdote is explained simply. A 15-year-old could follow the argument without prior knowledge of AI or regulation.

relevance.note: The reader is likely to reconsider how they evaluate truth in a world of deepfakes and corporate lies, and may become more skeptical of expert agencies and media. The action is not a direct personal decision like taking a pill, but it changes how the reader approaches information consumption and trust in institutions, which is a system they live inside.

quality.note: The piece is well-structured with a clear thesis, and each claim is supported with specific examples and links. However, the middle section on regulatory capture repeats the same point about compromised agencies multiple times, and the 'Hey look at this' and 'Object permanence' sections are pure link lists that could be cut without losing the core argument. Roughly a third could be trimmed.

zh.thesis: AI 制造的认知危机是一场“机会性感染”，它之所以致命，是因为我们的真相判断系统早已被大公司和监管俘获掏空。
zh.text:
AI 能造假视频、假语音，让名人说没说过的话，这的确吓人。但作者认为，AI 不是新敌人，它只是给一场老战争补了一刀。

## 1. 认知危机早就开始了

你没法亲自验证食品安不安全、房子牢不牢、刹车灵不灵，所以你信任专家机构。但这些机构早被大公司渗透了：药企高管进 FDA，FDA 的人出来当说客。作者说，疫苗该打，但别因为信任药厂才打。

## 2. 生活里全是“钓鱼”陷阱

银行打电话要你交个人信息，这不是诈骗，是银行教的；家人被捕要你打钱，因为监狱和医院真这么干；明星代言垃圾币，因为明星真这么干。这些事现在看都觉得正常，正是认知防线失守的证据。

## 3. 真相死了，AI 来收尸

普京的策略不是让你信假话，而是让你怀疑一切。AI 的深度伪造也一样，它让每个影像都可能是假的，于是真假不再重要。作者说，AI 是机会性感染，专挑免疫力低下的人下手。人类被大公司搞了几十年，认知免疫系统早垮了，AI 只是最后一击。

一句话：AI 骗不到你，除非你早就习惯被骗。

articles.title: Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence?
articles.titleZh: AI 的“聪明”可能只是错觉：像研究婴儿一样研究它
articles.author: Steven Strogatz and Janna Levin

substance.note: Mitchell argues that AI is an 'alien intelligence' and that we lack adequate methods for measuring machine cognition, proposing six principles for better assessment. The argument is built from multiple angles — developmental psychology, comparative psychology, the Clever Hans parable, and the competence/performance distinction — and the mechanism (spurious associations in benchmarks) generalizes to any field that evaluates AI by tasks, such as law or medicine.

surprise.note: The Clever Hans story is retold with a twist: the horse was a genius at reading social cues, not at math, and the parallel to AI benchmarks is striking. The claim that AI can answer diagram questions without seeing the diagrams is a specific, counterintuitive example worth mentioning.

accessible.note: The conversation is in plain language, with technical terms like 'mechanistic interpretability' explained on the spot. The Clever Hans story and the radiologist example make the ideas vivid for a non-specialist.

relevance.note: The reader will think differently about AI benchmarks and the hype around AI capabilities, but the article is more about a field than about the reader's own life. It might influence how they interpret AI news, but it doesn't prescribe a direct action.

quality.note: The podcast format is conversational and engaging, but the transcript includes lengthy host banter and repeated introductions that could be trimmed. The core ideas are clear, but the middle section on math and jobs meanders.

zh.thesis: 人工智能的“智能”与人类不同，现有的评测方法不可靠，需要用研究婴儿和动物的方法来科学地评估 AI。
zh.text:
当 AI 聊天机器人流利回答问题时，人们容易觉得它像人一样思考。但作者指出，AI 的运作方式与人类截然不同，更像一种“外星智能”。

如何评估这种陌生的智能？作者提出借鉴发展心理学和比较心理学的方法，就像研究婴儿和动物那样。以下是评估 AI 认知能力的六个原则：

## 1. 警惕“拟人化”偏见

人们看到 AI 说人话，就忍不住觉得它有情感、有意识。要意识到这种倾向，别被流畅的语言迷惑。

## 2. 科学地怀疑：做对照实验

就像“聪明的汉斯”那匹马，它能算数，但其实是阅读提问者的面部微表情。当 AI 答对问题时，需要排除侥幸和虚假关联，设计对照实验验证。

## 3. 换着花样测试泛化能力

用不同变体的问题测试 AI，看它是真正掌握原理，还是只会死记硬背。就像学生背下例题，换道题就不会做，那就是“表演”而非“能力”。

## 4. 别把 AI 当黑箱

AI 的内部结构可以被探测，类似神经科学的“机制可解释性”。研究它的激活和权重，有助于理解它真正在做什么。

## 5. 区分“表现”与“能力”

表现是特定任务上的输出，能力是潜在的理解。AI 可能靠捷径“作弊”答对，不等于具备相应能力。

## 6. 分析失败，拥抱负面结果

错误和失败往往比成功更能揭示本质。不要只报喜不报忧，负面结果同样是科学进步的养料。

最后，作者认为，AI 的发展不应只追求“完成任务”，而应追求真正的理解。就像数学难题被 AI 攻克，并不代表它拥有人类那样的创造力。科学地测评 AI，是让技术可靠、可控的关键一步。

articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 409 期）：程序员的职业未来
articles.titleZh: 程序员会被AI取代吗？未来可能只剩一种程序员

substance.note: The lead essay argues that software development is an industrial process and that AI coding agents will permanently reshape the profession, with specific predictions like the decline of niche languages and the rise of automated code quality standards. This is a contestable position argued from multiple angles, and the mechanism of industrialization generalizes to other knowledge work, but it does not reach a completely different domain.

surprise.note: The claim that AI will not eliminate programmers but will force them to work more intensively, and that manual coding will be restricted to hobbyists, contradicts the common belief that AI will either replace programmers or free them from drudgery. The specific prediction that niche languages like Zig and Haskell will be rewritten by AI into mainstream ones is a memorable, counterintuitive point.

accessible.note: The article is written for a general tech-interested audience, but it assumes familiarity with programming languages, coding agents, and software development workflows. Terms like 'coding agent' and 'LLM' are used without explanation, though the core argument about industrialization is clear to a non-programmer.

relevance.note: For a programmer, this article directly affects their career decisions — whether to learn niche languages, how to position themselves in the job market, and what skills to develop. For a non-programmer, it offers insight into the future of software and the economy, but the direct action is limited to those in the field.

quality.note: The article is well-structured with a clear lead essay followed by curated links, but the lead essay repeats its main point several times — that AI will increase programmer workload and reduce manual coding — and the 'LLM optimization' section feels like a tangent. The tech news items are concise, but some could be cut without loss.

zh.thesis: 软件开发的工业化趋势将使手工编码逐渐被淘汰，程序员的主要工作将转变为帮助和审查AI。
zh.text:
程序员这行以后会怎样？有人说AI会取代程序员，有人说不会。最近有个老外的预测，比较靠谱。

核心观点：大多数商业软件开发是工业流程，不是手工活。工业化要求提高效率、降低成本、保证质量。AI恰好符合这个要求，所以会被大规模采用。

## 1. AI编码代理将无处不在

AI大模型越来越强，编码代理也越来越强。公司会给程序员施压，让他们多用编码代理，想降低门槛、增加强度。最好销售也能开发软件。

## 2. 手工编码将被严格限制

代码质量将被量化，自动检测工具越来越多。大多数软件不该再手工写，那样经济上划不来。还想手工编码的，可能只能业余时间在家搞。

## 3. 程序员的活变成"帮AI"

程序员的主要工作，将变成帮AI变好：审查AI生成的代码、测试AI的更改、减少错误。行业标准越来越要求程序员多干活。

一句话总结：程序员不会消失，但手工编码会消失，剩下的程序员要转型为AI的"教练"和"质检员"。

articles.title: A dumpling shop becomes a poster child of AI adoption in China
articles.titleZh: 北京这家饺子馆，凭啥成了中国AI的“宣传委员”？
articles.author: Viola Zhou

substance.note: The piece argues that China's AI enthusiasm is a cultural and economic stance, using the dumpling shop owner as a concrete case, but the insight is mostly a contrast between Chinese and Western attitudes without a deeper mechanism that generalizes beyond the anecdote.

surprise.note: It highlights the counterintuitive fact that a small dumpling shop owner in China is eagerly adopting AI while Western small businesses hide their AI use, which is a specific and notable contrast.

accessible.note: The story is told through a human scene and plain language; the only technical term, 'AI agent', is explained in a few words, making it easy for a general reader to follow.

relevance.note: The reader is unlikely to change their own behavior, but the piece touches on a system they live inside—the global AI economy and cultural attitudes toward technology—making it feel relevant to their understanding of the world.

quality.note: The article is well-structured with a clear narrative arc, but the middle section repeats the contrast between Chinese and Western attitudes that was already established in the opening, and some details (like the token coupon) are mentioned without follow-up.

zh.thesis: 在中国，AI被视为必然趋势，连饺子馆老板都主动拥抱，与西方对AI的警惕形成鲜明对比。
zh.text:
北京一家叫「金谷园」的饺子馆，最近成了中国AI应用的「宣传委员」。老板李波搞了个「技能」，让顾客能用AI助手点餐、排队，还代码生成网站，甚至送Token券。

李波41岁，北邮电信工程硕士毕业，2010年没当工程师，反而开过青旅、卖过甜点，最后和饺子师傅合伙开了这家店。AI让他重新燃起对科技的热情。

「你们老觉得AI抢饭碗，我们却抢着用。」这是中国和西方的鲜明对比。作者发现，纽约小商家不敢承认用AI，怕像作弊；中国却人人抢学AI课，怕落后。

## 1. 老板的算盘：AI是先进生产力

李波引用邓小平名言：「科学技术是第一生产力。」他相信，未来人人都会让AI安排吃喝，饺子馆得先上车。「总要拥抱最先进的生产力。」

## 2. AI带来的热度＞实际使用

李波承认，这个AI技能带来的媒体关注比实际使用多。但他很骄傲，说：「总得有人先开始用，哪怕它还不够好。蒸汽机刚出来时，人们笑它不如马，但最后汽车赢了。」

一句话总结：在西方担忧AI时，中国小老板把AI当「军备竞赛」，抢着当吃螃蟹的人，这态度本身就耐人寻味。

articles.title: AI's Bar Mitzvah Moment: From Hype & Hope to Business Questions!
articles.titleZh: AI的成人礼：谈钱不伤感情

substance.note: The author builds a four-phase cycle of revolutionary change and applies it to AI, arguing that AI is in the 'business building' phase and must be judged by business fundamentals, not potential. He provides a framework with market size, industry economics, and moats, and uses reverse engineering to show that a $2 trillion Anthropic valuation requires $1.2 trillion in revenues. The framework is specific and contestable, but it does not generalize to a completely different domain.

surprise.note: The piece challenges the common belief that AI's huge market potential guarantees business success, pointing out that 'big markets don't always become big businesses.' It also reveals that the cost of producing AI tokens has dropped while the cost of accessing frontier models has risen, a counterintuitive paradox. However, there is no single sentence that a reader would repeat verbatim.

accessible.note: The article explains technical terms like TAM, ARR, and unit economics in plain language, and uses analogies like the 'bar mitzvah moment' and 'most expensive factory in history.' However, it assumes familiarity with financial concepts like market cap and operating margins, which may require some explanation for a general reader.

relevance.note: The reader is likely an investor or business person who will use the framework to evaluate AI companies and capital expenditures. The article provides a concrete tool (breakeven calculator) that could influence investment decisions, but for a general reader, the relevance is more intellectual than actionable.

quality.note: The article is well-structured with clear sections and data sources, but it is long and repetitive in places, especially in the discussion of market size and constraints. Some sections could be condensed without losing substance.

zh.thesis: AI虽潜力巨大，但当前估值远超实际收入，需按商业逻辑检验，而非只讲故事。
zh.text:
2022年ChatGPT横空出世，AI热潮烧了四年。英伟达市值飙升，七大科技巨头贡献美股45%涨幅，数据中心投资拉动美国GDP约1%。

但热闹背后，真正的问题不是AI多厉害，而是它能不能变成一门好生意。作者称之为AI的「成人礼」：投资者不再为梦想买单，要看到实打实的收入和利润。

## 1. 市场多大？先别做梦

AI企业最爱吹总市场规模（TAM）。某银行给xAI估了22万亿美元，作者觉得这是幻觉。目前AI年收入撑死2500亿美元，相比数万亿美元投资，杯水车薪。

AI的真实上限是员工薪酬。美国2025年全部员工薪酬约13万亿美元，AI不可能全吃掉——工具替代不了人，只有替换员工才有大市场。还得看定价、行业和地域。

## 2. 赚钱难在哪？

技术公司通常边际成本趋零，但AI不是。生成token要烧电、烧芯片，成本虽降，用量却涨。高端AI服务越来越贵，利润薄如刀片。

商业模式也在试错：订阅不划算，转向按用量付费；开放还是封闭模型，各有取舍。想赢，要么拼规模成本，要么拼技术壁垒，但没人保证赢。

## 3. 不光算账，还要看社会账

数据中心占地耗电，引发居民抗议；数据隐私惹人忧；高薪岗位被AI顶替，民众恐慌；贫富差距或进一步拉大。

这些约束会转成真金白银的成本：盖数据中心更贵，监管更严，甚至可能被课重税。投资者若视而不见，迟早被反噬。

别被故事迷惑。AI能不能值钱，要看十年后要赚多少才能回本——按目前估值，整个行业得赚5万亿到8万亿美元，难度极大。与其随波逐流，不如用这套框架，自己算笔账。

articles.title: Liminal Spaces, Transitional States: Alexander Ullom on “It Ends”
articles.titleZh: 无尽公路、尖叫人群：毕业后的‘人间地狱’
articles.author: Zachary Lee

substance.note: The interview argues that liminality and ritual are the generation's response to dissolved moral structures, and that silly questions are a new unifying truth — a position argued through the film's design and the director's personal testimony, though it never generalizes beyond the film's own themes.

surprise.note: Points out that the film's aspect ratio changes to reflect a tonal war between horror and hangout, and that arguing over a stupid hypothetical is 'the most important thing in the entire world' — a specific, quotable paradox worth mentioning.

accessible.note: The film's premise is explained in plain terms, and the few technical terms like 'aspect ratio' are self-explanatory in context; the interview's conversational tone makes it followable without having seen the film.

relevance.note: The reader who has felt the weight of modern meaninglessness or the pull of online desensitization will recognize their own experience in the director's words, but the piece offers no action to take — it is a reflection, not a call to change.

quality.note: The interview is well-edited and flows naturally, but several themes — liminality, desensitization, the dissolution of structures — recur across multiple answers, and a few exchanges could be trimmed without losing the core.

zh.thesis: 《It Ends》用一部恐怖公路片，映射了Z世代在失去传统人生目标后，陷入永恒过渡期的迷茫与挣扎。
zh.text:
导演亚历山大·乌洛姆的新片《It Ends》讲了个怪事：四个大学刚毕业的朋友，半夜开车上路，结果开进了一条永远没有尽头的公路。

他们每次停车休息，只能喘口气90秒，接着就会有一大群尖叫的人冲过来攻击他们。

## 1. 这不只是恐怖片，是‘成长’的比喻

乌洛姆说，这电影是‘宗教创伤’的隐喻——但别误会，他并不反对宗教。他只是觉得，现在年轻人失去了老一辈那些‘人生支柱’：成家、买房、信教，全都没了。

于是，所有人都卡在一种‘过渡状态’里，就像那条无尽公路。

## 2. 用‘仪式感’来对抗绝望

片子里，角色们发明了各种‘仪式’来熬过困境：尖叫，是把恐惧喊出来；刷梗图，是让大脑放空；跳舞，是反抗资本主义对情绪的压榨。

导演本人也有自己的‘仪式’——他现在会爬消防梯上天台晒太阳，或者重新开始读书，他说：‘其实大家都懂该做什么，难的是真的去做。’

## 3. ‘无聊的傻问题’反而是解药

电影里，角色们会为了‘100个人打得过一只大猩猩吗’这种问题吵上半天。乌洛姆觉得，这种没答案的蠢问题，其实就是现代人的‘精神寄托’。

既然世界上没有绝对真理了，那么和朋友争论一个假想题，反而成了最真实的连接。他说：‘这可能是我们这一代人，在没有宗教后，唯一能共同相信的东西。’

一句话总结：当一切意义都崩塌时，和你在乎的人瞎聊、瞎闹，可能就是唯一真实的救赎。

articles.title: It’s not the fault of right-wing news
articles.titleZh: 不是媒体的错：拉开你与家人距离的，是朋友圈
articles.author: Joachim Klement

substance.note: The piece argues that social circles, not media diet, drive polarisation, citing a specific Tinbergen Institute study and a chart, but the argument is a summary of that study's findings rather than a synthesis that generalises beyond the study's context.

surprise.note: It challenges the common belief that cable news is the main driver of polarisation, offering the counterintuitive claim that your social circle matters more, but there is no single sentence that would be repeated verbatim.

accessible.note: The topic is political polarisation, which is familiar to most readers, and the only technical term is 'Tinbergen Institute', which is not explained but does not hinder understanding.

relevance.note: The reader lives inside the polarised society described and may reconsider how their own social circle shapes their views, but the piece does not prescribe a specific action.

quality.note: The piece is concise and the study is named, but the opening restates the common view at length before getting to the study, and the final paragraph repeats the point about social bubbles.

zh.thesis: 研究发现，导致政治极化的主要因素不是媒体，而是社交圈的同质化。
zh.text:
美国社会越来越撕裂，很多人第一反应是怪媒体，尤其是福克斯新闻、MSNBC 这些频道，觉得它们天天带节奏。

但荷兰丁伯根研究所的新研究说：冤枉媒体了。真正的“元凶”是社交圈。

## 1. 换新闻，不如换邻居

研究显示，换新闻来源，对人们的气候变化看法几乎没影响。可如果社交圈稍微变一下，看法就差远了。

甚至可以说：你对气候的态度，更多取决于你住在哪个县，而不是你看哪个台。

## 2. 圈子越杂，人越开明

社交环境越多元——不同种族、教育、年龄、党派的人混在一起——就越容易碰到不同观点，这样政治极化会减轻，对气候变化的担忧反而增加。

要是天天只跟自己相似的人待着，观点就会越来越偏，思维也越来越封闭。

## 3. 左右都一样

这个规律不分左右，无论哪个阵营，圈子越封闭，想法就越极端。

一句话：让观点走极端的，不是屏幕里的主播，而是身边缺乏不同声音的朋友圈。

articles.title: College EA Meetups Everywhere: Call For Organizers
articles.titleZh: 大学EA聚会招募：当个组织者，一起改变世界
articles.author: Scott Alexander

substance.note: The piece is a call to action with practical guidance, but the core argument — that college EA groups need organizers and that anyone can do it — is a position argued from a single line of reasoning (the bottleneck is people, not money) and the rest is logistics. The mechanism of 'minimum viable effort' generalizes to other volunteer recruitment, but it's not deeply explored.

surprise.note: The surprising claim is that you don't need any qualifications to organize a meetup — 'If you can put a name/time/date in a box on Google Forms and show up there, you have the minimum skill necessary' — which contradicts the common belief that organizing requires experience or charisma. That sentence is worth repeating.

accessible.note: The piece is written in plain language with no jargon; terms like 'EA' and 'ACX' are used but explained implicitly through context, and the advice is concrete and easy to follow for anyone, including a 15-year-old.

relevance.note: For a reader who is a college student or near a campus, this could prompt them to start a meetup — that's a concrete action. But for most readers, it's about a niche movement they don't belong to, so it's interesting but detached.

quality.note: The piece is well-organized with clear FAQ sections, but the middle repeats the same points (how to sign up, what to do, who can organize) multiple times in different forms. Roughly a third could be cut without losing anything.

zh.thesis: 在大学办一场EA聚会，是让聪明人投身AI安全等事业的最简单起点。
zh.text:
每年春秋，作者都会帮各地的ACX聚会做宣传。今年夏天，重点转向大学的「有效利他」（EA）社团。很多大学已有这类团体，但更多学校还没有。作者想招募志愿者，在自家学校办一场EA见面会。

为什么这么急？因为AGI的时钟在滴答作响，AI新贵们捐了大笔钱，现在缺的不是资金，而是能把钱变成好结果的聪明人。这些人可能正忙着别的事，所以作者来招募读者。

## 1. 当组织者到底要干啥

最低要求：填个表格，写上时间地点，到时候举着牌子出现就行。不需要是学生，研究生、老师、附近居民都可以。

聚会内容很简单：大家来了就聊天。可以准备些话题卡，比如「你最近对什么兴奋？」在名牌上写兴趣，热情打招呼。别搞强制活动，也别拼命拉人入坑。

## 2. 怎么让聚会不翻车

时间选在九月中旬到十月底之间，最好避开期中考试和开学周。校园里工作日晚比周末效果好，因为学生周末常回家或有事。

地点要方便找、不太吵、能有座位和厕所。教室、学生活动室、图书馆讨论间都行。别选酒吧，很多本科生不到合法喝酒年龄。

## 3. 会有多少人？会一直当下去吗？

人数从零到五十都有可能。就算只来三个人，也是个完美的开始。如果担心没人来，带本书或朋友去。

作者澄清：办一次就够，不想续就忘掉。但很多人会因此成为常任组织者。想转正的话，可以收集大家的邮箱，用不是学校邮箱的地址，因为毕业后学校邮箱会失效。

赞助方Nest会报销名牌、披萨等费用，还提供建议。作者和另一位组织者也会帮忙。填表后就能获得支持。

总之，如果你的大学还没有EA团体，不妨考虑当个组织者。这是让聪明人聚在一起、可能改变世界的最简单方式。

articles.title: You’re Not a Universal Mosquito Magnet
articles.titleZh: 蚊子不挑人？新研究：你只是对特定种类有吸引力
articles.author: Jake Currie

substance.note: The article reports a study's findings that different mosquito species prefer different people based on skin microbiome, but it mostly relays the study's results without adding a deeper synthesis or generalizable mechanism beyond the specific findings.

surprise.note: It overturns the common belief that some people are universally attractive to mosquitoes, revealing that attractiveness is species-specific, but the key insight is stated plainly without a memorable quotable sentence.

accessible.note: The article explains technical terms like 'volatile organic compounds' and 'microbiome' in plain language, and the experiment is described in a way that requires no prior knowledge of entomology.

relevance.note: The reader might reconsider their mosquito repellent strategy or understand why they get bitten more in certain areas, but the article does not prompt a specific action beyond general awareness.

quality.note: The article is concise and well-structured, but it repeats the main finding about species-specific attraction multiple times, and some sections like the related stories list could be trimmed without loss.

zh.thesis: 没有谁是所有蚊子的最爱，但每个人至少会吸引某一种蚊子，这跟皮肤上的细菌有关。
zh.text:
夏天被蚊子咬得满腿包，总觉得自己是“蚊子磁铁”？新研究说，你可能不是所有蚊子的菜，但至少是某一种的“心头好”。

研究者让119个人把手臂伸进装满蚊子的管子（有网隔着，不会被咬），记录每种蚊子扑向谁。结果发现：没有一个人对三种蚊子都有吸引力，但所有人都至少让一种蚊子疯狂。

## 1. 皮肤细菌决定你的“蚊子缘”

蚊子闻的不是你的血，而是你皮肤上细菌产生的气味。每个人的皮肤细菌组合不同，所以气味也不同。

研究者发现，某种细菌让库蚊避之不及，而另一些细菌则让白纹伊蚊兴奋不已，比如酮类（爱生酮饮食的人注意了）和植物味化合物。

## 2. 不同蚊子，不同口味

埃及伊蚊偏爱男性，因为男性皮肤细菌产生的脂肪酸气味更多。而三种蚊子都对一种果香味物质情有独钟，这物质还常用在香水里。

每种蚊子都有自己的“美食清单”，这说明它们在演化上走了不同的路，各自解码人类的“气味签名”。

研究者说，搞清楚这些化学线索，就能研发更有效的驱蚊剂。快一点吧，夏天等不起！

articles.title: Data Center Spending in US
articles.titleZh: 美国数据中心建设狂潮：是福是祸？
articles.author: conversableeconomist

substance.note: The piece argues that opposition to data centers is largely misguided and that AI's negative framing is overblown, but the argument is mostly a series of assertions and examples rather than a deep synthesis; the mechanism of data center spending driving blue-collar work and the comparison to other IT industries is interesting but not fully developed.

surprise.note: The claim that data center construction spending is on track to hit $40 billion in 2026 is a specific number worth mentioning, and the point that AI has the worst PR campaign ever is a fresh angle, but the overall argument that data centers are not inherently bad is not particularly counterintuitive.

accessible.note: The article is written in plain language with minimal jargon; terms like 'on-site construction spending' are self-explanatory, and the reference to 'AI slop' is colloquial, making it easy for a general reader to follow.

relevance.note: The reader is unlikely to take a specific action, but the topic touches on the economy, technology, and local politics, which are systems the reader lives inside; the mention of potential health benefits from AI adds a personal stake, though it is not directly actionable.

quality.note: The piece is a blog post that meanders from data to political commentary to AI PR to health research, with several tangents that could be cut; the repeated 'maybe, just maybe' phrasing and the shift to the Works in Progress essay feel like padding, so roughly a third could be removed without losing the core point.

zh.thesis: 美国数据中心建设支出飙升，反对者应理性看待其经济价值和AI潜力。
zh.text:
美国数据中心建设支出正在飙升，仅现场施工费用就可能在2026年达到400亿美元。这一趋势从2023年初开始加速，至今未见放缓迹象。

## 1. 数据中心建设为何火爆？

数据中心支撑着从流媒体到云存储的无数在线服务，AI的崛起更是推波助澜。建设浪潮带来大量蓝领工作，对当地经济是实实在在的利好。

## 2. 反对声音站得住脚吗？

反对者担忧能源、水、噪音和交通问题，但这些是任何工业项目都会面临的。若因反对AI而阻碍数据中心建设，不如直接限制芯片或智能手机生产——这显然不现实。

## 3. AI的潜在好处被低估

AI的负面宣传铺天盖地，但AI辅助医疗研究可能加速治愈疾病，延长人类寿命。与其盲目抵制，不如权衡利弊，拥抱技术进步。

总之，数据中心建设是数字化时代的必然趋势，反对者应理性看待其价值与挑战。

articles.title: 我的博客如何改变了一个人的命运？
articles.titleZh: 一条博客留言，改变了一个人的投资人生

substance.note: The article is essentially a testimonial from a reader, quoted at length, praising the author's blog for changing his investment approach. The author adds little beyond framing and thanks; the core content is the reader's own story, not an original argument or mechanism.

surprise.note: The only mildly surprising element is that a blog could change someone's financial trajectory, but this is a familiar anecdote in the personal finance blogging world, and the article confirms rather than overturns expectations.

accessible.note: The article is written in plain language, with terms like '定投' (dollar-cost averaging) and '标普和纳指100' (S&P and Nasdaq 100) used without explanation, but the overall narrative is easy to follow for a general reader.

relevance.note: For readers interested in personal finance or investing, the article might reinforce the value of long-term index investing, but it offers no new actionable insight; it is essentially a success story that is interesting but detached from the reader's own decisions.

quality.note: The article is mostly a long quote from a comment, with the author's own text limited to a brief introduction and thanks. The structure is simple, but the content is repetitive—the reader's praise is echoed in the comments, and the article could be cut by half without losing anything.

zh.thesis: 一个普通网友因读到一篇博客文章，从害怕股市到重仓美股，最终获得丰厚回报，人生轨迹因此改变。
zh.text:
有位叫「阿迪2000」的网友，旅居日本。他原本在国内炒A股，2015年及时退出，赚了几十万，从此对股市心有余悸，觉得炒股不可能赚钱。

到了海外，他也不敢开户。直到2023年底，他在文学城读到一篇关于高中生冒雪返乡的博文，被作者的文笔打动，一口气读完了他的全部文章。

## 一顿阅读，打通了投资任督二脉

原来，这位博主是清华毕业的计算机博士，一直在教大家定投美股指数。阿迪这才明白：难赚钱的是A股，其他市场也可以投资。

从2018到2023年底，他几乎没有投资收入，而投资美股的朋友资产翻倍。于是2024年，他开了账户，几乎把所有钱投入市场；2025年，又用卖房的钱买了A股里的标普和纳指100指数。

## 账户涨了30%到90%

如今，他的账户根据产品和时间不同，有了30%到90%的利润。更重要的是，他认同了博主的长期投资理念。

这位博主就是「硅谷居士」。阿迪感叹：虽然错过了19到23年的五年，但有幸认识居士，可以说改变了我的人生走向。

## 免费分享，改变人生

硅谷居士写博客纯粹是免费分享，他的书还有免费版，估计上百万人看过。他不仅教投资，还常帮网友解答疑惑，把投资理念用几句话讲清楚。

网友留言说，居士的分享改变了很多人，有人因此提早实现退休。可见，好的分享真的能改变命运。

substance.note: The article reports on a study showing mussels reduce filtration in response to predator cues, but it mostly relays the findings without a deeper synthesis or a mechanism that generalizes beyond this case.

surprise.note: It reveals the unexpected fact that mussels respond to harmless snails as a warning sign, which is a specific and counterintuitive detail worth mentioning.

accessible.note: The subject is explained in plain language with minimal jargon; terms like 'inhalant siphon' are described in context, making it easy for a general reader to follow.

relevance.note: The article is interesting but detached from the reader's daily life; it concerns marine ecology and has no direct action the reader would take.

quality.note: The article is concise and well-structured, but it repeats the key finding about filtration reduction multiple times and includes promotional content that could be cut.

rejected.title: The Intellectual Circle Jerk and Why We Can't Stop

substance.note: Argues that intellectual culture rewards agreement over challenge and that this produces a monoculture, but the mechanism (network effects) is described rather than demonstrated with evidence, and the argument never generalizes beyond the author's own field of media and publishing.

surprise.note: Points at the unnoticed cost of confirmation-seeking in intellectual life, but the claim that we read to feel smart is familiar to most informed readers, and there is no single sentence worth repeating verbatim.

accessible.note: Uses plain language throughout, with only a few terms like 'p-hacked' and 'monoculture' that are explained in context or are common enough for a general reader.

relevance.note: The reader is invited to change their reading habits and to seek out stronger opposing views, but the action is vague and the piece does not connect to a system the reader lives inside beyond their own media consumption.

quality.note: The piece is well-written and has a clear structure, but the middle section repeats the opening argument in different words, and the final paragraph explicitly acknowledges the irony that the piece itself will be shared among those who agree, which undercuts its own point.

substance.note: The piece is a personal travelogue with observations about Manhattan's contrasts, but it offers no contestable position or transferable mechanism; the insights are anecdotal and stay within the walk itself.

surprise.note: It points at unnoticed details like the world's worst Starbucks and the survival of historic blocks, but these are fleeting and not likely to be repeated verbatim.

accessible.note: No technical jargon; the narrative is plain and easy to follow, though some local references (POPS, Fraunces Tavern) are unexplained.

relevance.note: The reader has no stake in this walk; it is a detached travelogue with no action or system they live inside.

quality.note: The piece is well-written but padded with many asides and name-drops that could be cut without loss; roughly a third is extraneous.

rejected.title: 'Darth Vader' Wants Flock in San Diego

substance.note: The piece is a brief news item relaying that someone dressed as Darth Vader spoke at a San Diego council meeting in support of Flock surveillance cameras; it offers no independent analysis, argument, or mechanism beyond the anecdote itself.

surprise.note: The only surprising element is the image of Darth Vader at a city council meeting, but the piece does not develop it into a larger insight or a quotable line; it is a curiosity that fades quickly.

accessible.note: The article is entirely plain language and requires no background knowledge; anyone can follow the anecdote, though the reference to Flock cameras is not explained.

relevance.note: The reader has no stake in a San Diego council meeting or in Flock's local rollout; it is a detached oddity with no action or system the reader touches.

quality.note: The piece is short and to the point, but it is padded with subscription prompts and a call for tips that could be cut; the core anecdote is thin and the article ends abruptly.

rejected.title: Kagi added a setting for removing paywalled links from search results

substance.note: The article is a changelog of Kagi updates, with no argument or synthesis; the only substantive item is the new paywall-link setting, but it is merely listed without any analysis or mechanism.

surprise.note: The paywall setting is a small novelty for Kagi users, but it is not counter-intuitive and nothing here would be worth repeating at a dinner table.

accessible.note: The text is plain and jargon-light, but it assumes familiarity with Kagi's product ecosystem and its feature names; a non-user would struggle to care.

relevance.note: Only relevant to Kagi users who might change their search settings; for everyone else it is a product update with no stake.

quality.note: The piece is a list of fixes and features with no narrative; many entries are redundant or trivial, and the whole could be cut to a single line about the paywall setting.

substance.note: This is a technical reference document that relays API usage details without any original synthesis or argument; the author's contribution is purely organizational, and the mechanism described (image tokenization) is not generalized to any other domain.

surprise.note: There is no counter-intuitive claim or hidden mechanism; it is a straightforward how-to guide that confirms what an informed reader would expect from an API reference.

accessible.note: The piece is dense with API jargon (base64, file_id, content blocks, endpoints) and assumes familiarity with OpenAI-compatible APIs; a non-practitioner could not follow or retell it.

relevance.note: This is relevant only to developers actively using this specific API; the reader has no stake unless they are building with this model, which is a niche hobbyist or professional interest.

quality.note: The structure is clear and the limits are tabulated, but the piece repeats the same three methods across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Responses APIs, and much could be cut without losing information.
